children.title: What can you reach with cu + dv?
children.summary: Drags the sliders c and d: two independent vectors fill the plane, two parallel ones only a line (spec below)
children.spec: Combine: drag c and d; the tip of cu + dv paints the set of reachable points. Independent versus dependent: rotate v onto u's line and the painted plane collapses to a line. Three vectors in 3D: add w; it either fills space or stays in the plane of u and v. Link: the same picture is the column space of the matrix [u v w].

children.title: Why is v · w = |v||w| cos θ?
children.summary: Rotates w around v; the dot product tracks the shadow length (see Trigonometry → Vectors)

children.title: Why can't |v · w| exceed |v||w|?
children.summary: Sees the shadow can never be longer than the vector (Schwarz inequality)

children.title: Why is Ax a combination of A's columns?
children.summary: Multiplies by columns: x₁ × column 1 + x₂ × column 2

children.title: Unit vectors and normalising
children.summary: Divides by the length and sees the arrow land on the unit circle

children.title: Row picture versus column picture
children.summary: Sees the same 2 × 2 system as two crossing lines, or as a combination of columns reaching b

children.title: Why does elimination fail, and when does a row swap rescue it?
children.summary: Hits a zero pivot; a swap fixes it unless the matrix is singular

children.title: Why is elimination the same as A = LU?
children.summary: Records each multiplier and finds they fill L exactly

children.title: Elimination matrices
children.summary: Multiplies by E₂₁, E₃₁, E₃₂ and watches A become U

children.title: Transposes and permutations
children.summary: Flips across the diagonal and reorders rows with P

children.title: Why do computers pick the largest pivot?
children.summary: Solves a system with a tiny pivot and watches rounding error explode (partial pivoting)

children.title: Four ways to multiply AB
children.summary: Sees AB as row·column, A × columns, rows × B, and a sum of column × row pieces, all giving the same answer

children.title: Why is (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹?
children.summary: Undoes the last operation first: socks and shoes

children.title: Why does a zero combination of columns kill the inverse?
children.summary: Finds Ax = 0 with x ≠ 0, so no inverse can bring back x

children.title: Gauss–Jordan for A⁻¹
children.summary: Row-reduces [A I] to [I A⁻¹] (see Systems & Matrices → Matrix Algebra)

children.title: What is a subspace?
children.summary: Tests lines and planes through the origin versus ones that miss it; closure under + and × decides

children.title: Why is every solution of Ax = b = particular + nullspace?
children.summary: Slides the nullspace line through one particular solution

children.title: Why do independent columns mean a unique solution?
children.summary: Adds a dependent column and sees a whole line of solutions appear

children.title: Why is the dimension the number of pivots?
children.summary: Reduces to R and counts the pivot and free columns: r + (n − r) = n

children.title: Why is the row space ⟂ the nullspace?
children.summary: Sees Ax = 0 means x is orthogonal to every row: the big picture of the four subspaces

children.title: Find all four subspaces
children.summary: Takes a 3 × 4 matrix to its bases for C(A), N(A), C(Aᵀ) and N(Aᵀ)

children.title: Basis and dimension
children.summary: Picks bases for a plane in many ways; the count stays 2

children.title: Why is projection the closest point?
children.summary: Drops a perpendicular from b onto a line and onto a plane; the error is ⟂ the target

children.title: Why is P² = P?
children.summary: Projects twice and nothing more moves

children.title: Why do orthonormal bases make everything easy?
children.summary: Sees Qᵀ = Q⁻¹ and coordinates become dot products

children.title: Gram–Schmidt
children.summary: Straightens a skewed basis one vector at a time

children.title: Why does AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb give the best fit?
children.summary: Sees no exact solution exists, so it projects b onto the column space (see Functions & Graphs → Modelling with Data)

children.title: Why are the errors ⟂ the columns?
children.summary: Checks that the residual is orthogonal to the 1s column and the x column

children.title: Fit lines and parabolas
children.summary: Fits several models by least squares and compares the errors

children.title: Weighted least squares
children.summary: Trusts some measurements more by weighting them

children.title: Why is det the volume scale factor?
children.summary: Watches a unit square or cube transform into a parallelogram or box (see Systems & Matrices → Determinants)

children.title: Why do the three basic properties decide everything?
children.summary: Derives det from det I = 1, the sign flip on a row swap, and linearity in each row

children.title: Why is det(AB) = det A · det B?
children.summary: Composes two area-scalings

children.title: Permutations and cofactors
children.summary: Expands the big formula with signs

children.title: Cramer's rule and A⁻¹ from cofactors
children.summary: Sees each formula as a ratio of determinants

children.title: Which vectors keep their direction?
children.summary: Spins a vector around while A acts; eigenvectors only stretch (spec below)
children.spec: Sweep: a vector x rotates around the unit circle while Ax is drawn; the two line up only at eigenvectors. Ellipse: the whole circle maps to an ellipse; for symmetric A its axes are the eigenvectors. Powers: apply A repeatedly and any vector turns toward the dominant eigenvector. Cases: shear (one eigenvector), rotation (no real ones) and projection (λ = 0 and 1).

children.title: Why is det(A − λI) = 0 the eigenvalue test?
children.summary: Sees A − λI must squash some vector to 0

children.title: Why do powers Aᵏ become easy?
children.summary: Diagonalises A = XΛX⁻¹, so Aᵏ = XΛᵏX⁻¹

children.title: Why do Fibonacci numbers grow like 1.618ⁿ?
children.summary: Writes the recurrence as a 2 × 2 matrix; its larger eigenvalue is the golden ratio

children.title: Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors
children.summary: Uses trace and determinant shortcuts for 2 × 2

children.title: Systems of differential equations
children.summary: Solves du/dt = Au with e^(λt) modes (see Differential Equations)

children.title: Why do symmetric matrices have perpendicular eigenvectors?
children.summary: Sees a symmetric map stretch along orthogonal axes, so the circle becomes an aligned ellipse

children.title: Why is 'positive definite' a bowl?
children.summary: Plots xᵀAx as a surface: bowl, saddle or trough (see Multivariable Calculus → Max, Min & Lagrange)

children.title: Five tests for positive definite
children.summary: Checks eigenvalues, pivots, upper-left determinants, energy and AᵀA

children.title: Why is every matrix rotate → stretch → rotate?
children.summary: Watches the unit circle become an ellipse in three moves: A = UΣVᵀ

children.title: Why can a few singular values rebuild an image?
children.summary: Keeps rank k of a photo and watches it sharpen as k grows

children.title: Bases in the SVD
children.summary: Finds the v's and u's from AᵀA and AAᵀ

children.title: Principal component analysis
children.summary: Finds the direction of most spread in a cloud of data points

children.title: What makes a transformation linear?
children.summary: Tests T(cu + dv) = cT(u) + dT(v) on rotations, shears and translations; translation fails

children.title: Why does every linear map have a matrix?
children.summary: Records where the basis vectors go; those images are the columns

children.title: Why does a good basis make the matrix simple?
children.summary: Changes to the eigenvector basis and the matrix turns diagonal

children.title: Hermitian and unitary matrices
children.summary: Sees the complex versions of symmetric and orthogonal

children.title: The fast Fourier transform
children.summary: Sees why splitting in halves turns n² work into n log n

children.title: Why does a Markov chain settle down?
children.summary: Repeats a transition matrix; λ = 1 gives the steady state and the other eigenvalues fade

children.title: Why are ill-conditioned systems dangerous?
children.summary: Nudges b slightly in a nearly singular system and watches x jump (condition number)

children.title: Graphs and networks
children.summary: Builds an incidence matrix and solves for currents on a small network

children.title: Springs and trusses: K = AᵀCA
children.summary: Sees the stiffness matrix assembled from springs in a line

children.title: Fourier series as linear algebra
children.summary: Treats sines as orthogonal 'vectors' for functions (see Trigonometry → Waves & Oscillations)

children.title: Computer graphics with 4 × 4 matrices
children.summary: Uses homogeneous coordinates so translation becomes a matrix

children.title: Matrix cryptography
children.summary: Encodes and decodes with a matrix mod 26

children.title: Covariance matrices
children.summary: Sees how two measurements vary together, drawn as an ellipse
